## Patched files

Vendored files altered by a `patches:` entry in `vendor.yml`. These are the only generated files that are not byte-identical to their source mod. A patch whose `from` text stops matching fails the build rather than reverting silently.

| File | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `common/governments/civics/pd_origins_unique.txt` | PD - Unique Worlds | PD gates two origins on `NOT = { value = CRYO }`, but the CRYO species class is declared by NOTHING -- not by PD, not by any other source in this manifest, not by vanilla. It belongs to a PD companion mod we do not harvest. The engine reports `Invalid government species_class reference [CRYO]` and the clause is dead either way: with no species ever of class CRYO the NOT is always true, so deleting the line is behaviour-identical. Declaring a stub class instead (decision 30) would be wrong here -- nothing references CRYO for art, so a stub would be a phantom species class that exists only to satisfy a test that can never fail. |
| `common/section_templates/!!!_sbx_3_0_starbase_sections.txt` | Starbase Extended 3.0 | SBX's CITADEL_STARBASE_SECTION replaces vanilla's (its `!!!_` prefix wins FIOS) and renumbers vanilla's oddly-named MEDIUM_GUN_010..013 to the conventional two-digit 10..12, one slot short. Vanilla's OWN biogenesis hatchery design still asks for 010..013, so four of its thirteen medium mounts did not exist -- `invalid component slot` x4 in the 2026-08-07 run. This renames SBX's 10/11/12 back to vanilla's 010/011/012 and adds the 013 SBX never had, restoring vanilla's exact thirteen slot names. Nothing else in either tree references a citadel MEDIUM_GUN by name, and SBX's STRONGHOLD/HEADQUARTERS _XL sections (which already run to 16 and 20 and are SBX's own) are deliberately untouched. Every slot in this section shares locatorname "medium_gun_01", so the added slot needs no new locator and cannot fire from the hull centre (decision 26). See .docs/decisions/37-sbx-citadel-slot-renumbering.md. |
| `common/ship_sizes/nsc_starbases.txt` | Starbase Extended 3.0 | This file uses @build_block_radius_starbase and @starbase_formation_priority at four sites but defines neither -- the definitions sit in its sibling sbx_3_0_starbases.txt, and `@` variables in Stellaris script are file-scoped. 4.4 reports `Malformed token` four times (E22 of the 2026-08-02 analysis, filed there under ASB Ironman; it is SBX's), and the two tiers this file exists to declare -- starbase_stronghold and starbase_headquarters, SBX's only NEW ship sizes -- get no build-block radius and no formation priority. Both lines are copied verbatim from sbx_3_0_starbases.txt, which agrees with vanilla's 00_starbases.txt on the values (20 and 1). Nothing invented. |
| `common/starbase_buildings/sbx_3_0_starbase_buildings.txt` | Starbase Extended 3.0 | `category` is a field of a `resources` block, not a trigger. financial_space_center has one copy-pasted into its `potential` block, where 4.4 tries to resolve it as a scripted trigger and reports `Error in scripted trigger, cannot find: category`. This file uses the line correctly 45 other times inside `resources` and those are left alone -- the anchor includes the `potential = {` opener, which is unique. |
| `common/starbase_modules/sbx_3_0_orbital_ring_modules.txt` | Starbase Extended 3.0 | `orbital_ring_missile_battery` declares `potential` twice; 4.4 keeps one and drops the other. The second block's conditions are folded into the first and the duplicate removed, so both the gate and the build-count cap apply. Lines moved, not rewritten. |
| `common/starbase_modules/sbx_3_0_starbase_modules.txt` | Starbase Extended 3.0 | SBX carries New Ship Classes compatibility hooks: conditional output gated on `has_starbase_building = mining_manager` / `assembly_line_manufacturing`, both NSC buildings. NSC is not in the harvest, so the key resolves against nothing and 4.4 reports `Failed to deferred read key reference` five times. The blocks are dead weight -- a trigger on a building that cannot exist never fires -- so removing them is behaviour-identical and costs no output any starbase could actually have earned. |
| `events/!!!!!!ariphaos_precursor_cosmic.txt` | Assorted Precursor Adjustments | cstorms.200 targets add_anomaly at `owner` from inside `from = { ... }`, which is the surveyed planet -- and its own trigger requires that planet to be uncolonised, so the country never resolves. Restore vanilla's `root.owner`, the surveying ship's owner, which is the country the sibling event cstorms.100 already targets. |
| `events/pd_aw_planetary_infesters_events.txt` | PD - Ascension Worlds | The Ascension Worlds copy of the same three events, with the same defect. |
| `events/pd_planetary_infesters_events.txt` | Planetary Diversity | planet_event on on_building_complete / on_building_upgraded is an unsupported scope; vanilla uses carrier_event on both. |
| `events/realspace_game_start.txt` | Real Space 4.0 | Real Space's start menu (realspace.204 -> realspace.206) is a popup on every new game offering settings STG never changes. Fire the apply event realspace.1000 directly instead, which is what closing the menu does. |
| `gfx/models/combat_items/_ballistics_entities_ap.asset` | ASB Ironman | @plasmasmallplasmuzzle / @plasmamedium... / @plasmalarge... are never defined; the intended variables are @smallplasmuzzle / @mediumplasmuzzle / @largeplasmuzzle, defined at the top of this same file and already used by the parallel plasma_accelerator entities. No values invented. |
| `gfx/models/combat_items/_ballistics_entities_disr.asset` | ASB Ironman | `volume` is not a valid key in a 4.4 entity sound block; vanilla never uses it. 12 disruptor muzzle and distance-fire events, all identical. |
| `gfx/models/planets/_pd_unihabitable_entities.asset` | Planetary Diversity | `gas_giant_saturn_entity` was declared by this file AND by Real Space's rs_planetary_entities.asset, with bodies that differ: PD paints it with gas_giant_saturn_diffuse.dds at scale 1.2, Real Space with gas_giant_31_diffuse.dds at @gas_giant_scale (= 1). The engine keeps one and logs the other, and which one it keeps is recorded nowhere -- so this silently decided what Saturn looks like on every Sol start. 2026-08-07. REAL SPACE WINS, because it owns the name: all six solar_system_initializers that place this entity are Real Space's (sol, sol_solsector_small/large, federations, pre_ftl, unplugged), at size = 35 / has_ring = yes, and @gas_giant_scale is the variable keeping its other gas giants consistent. PD's 1.2 would have made Saturn 20% larger than the system built around it. RENAMED, NOT DELETED. PD's art stays in the tree under a name nothing places, so switching to it later is a one-line change rather than a re-harvest. Nothing dangles: PD's own events/pd_engine.txt still says `set_planet_entity = { entity = "gas_giant_saturn_entity" }`, which Real Space declares -- and that event gates on planet_size = 30 where Real Space's Sol builds Saturn at 35, so it is unlikely to fire here at all. See .docs/decisions/31-duplicate-entity-declarations.md. |

| `gfx/particles/_ships_particles.gfx` | ASB Ironman | DECISION 07's FAILURE MODE, IN A MOD THAT IS NOT STNH. ASB's copy of this vanilla file is the 3.x one, so it declares 151 of vanilla 4.4's 155 ship particles and silently drops four: astral_rift_particle, astral_scar_particle, crystal_rift_particle (Astral Planes) and ship_burn_particle_timed. All four are still referenced by vanilla files that load normally, so an astral rift renders with no particle at all -- `Couldn't find particle 3D object`, four of the 127 in the 2026-08-02 log. The four blocks below are vanilla 4.4's, copied verbatim. |
| `gfx/particles/combat/adv_kinetic_artillery_muzzle.asset` | ASB Ironman | Five-value "grow" curve -- see the banner above. The missing final value is restored as 1.000; no existing number is changed or dropped. |
| `gfx/particles/combat/adv_kinetic_artillery_shield_hit_effect.asset` | ASB Ironman | ASB typo -- the animation block is spelled "nimation", so 4.4 rejects the token and drops the rest of the effect. One occurrence per file. |
| `gfx/particles/combat/arc_emitter_muzzle.asset` | ASB Ironman | Five-value "grow" curve -- see the banner above. The missing final value is restored as 1.000; no existing number is changed or dropped. |
| `gfx/particles/combat/arc_emitter_muzzle_windup_effect.asset` | ASB Ironman | Five-value "grow" curve -- see the banner above. The missing final value is restored as 1.000; no existing number is changed or dropped. |
| `gfx/particles/combat/arc_trail_effect.asset` | ASB Ironman | JUDGEMENT, NOT RECONSTRUCTION. The curve has SEVEN values, so it does not divide into (time, value) pairs at all, and its times read 0.000 0.000 1.000. The animation is a 10 ms "grow2" spike, so the intended shape is unambiguous -- rise to 1 and fall back to 0 -- but the midpoint time was typed as 0.000 and a stray eighth value is missing. Rewritten as a symmetric spike, 0.000 0.000 / 0.500 1.000 / 1.000 0.000. Any midpoint in (0,1) works; 0.500 is a choice. Today the curve is rejected outright and the property is not animated at all, so this is strictly better than the status quo -- but change it freely if the effect looks wrong in game. |
| `gfx/particles/combat/auto_cannons_small_muzzle_bullets_effect.asset` | ASB Ironman | SUBSTITUTION, NOT RECONSTRUCTION -- the weakest patch here, flagged as such. The curve has FIVE values (1.000 0.706 0.564 0.150 0.000): an odd count that cannot pair, with times descending whichever way you read it. Reversing it does not close the pairs either, so the author's intent is not recoverable. Replaced with a plain 1 -> 0 decay, which is what a muzzle flash alpha does and what the surviving numbers trend towards. The alternative is leaving a curve the engine rejects outright, which animates nothing. If ASB ever fixes this the patch will fail the build and you can simply delete it. |

The faction's own command top is kept rather than prime Starfleet's security top: this folder exists to make the Confederation look unlike Starfleet, and the row is one of many gated on `uses_confed_corps_uniform`. See .docs/decisions/80-selector-textures-that-resolve.md. |
| `gfx/projectiles/alt_strike_craft_weapons.txt` | ASB Ironman | `shield_impact` accepts size small, medium or big; this one says `none`, so 4.4 rejects it and the strike-craft shield hit plays no effect at all. Vanilla's own strike_craft_weapons.txt uses `small` for every strike craft, which is the value taken here. |
| `gfx/projectiles/ap_missiles.txt` | ASB Ironman | max_duration is valid on projectile_gfx_ballistic in vanilla 4.4 -- 79 uses across 10 files -- and on no other projectile type. ASB puts it on a projectile_gfx_missile block, where 4.4 rejects it. Removed; @maxduration is left defined and simply unused, since ASB may reference it again. |
| `interface/zzz_sbx_3_0_starbase_view.gui` | Starbase Extended 3.0 | SBX's starbase view replaces vanilla's `design_info` window but omits the `design_name` instantTextBoxType the game writes the selected design's name into. 4.4 reports `Could not find instantTextboxType design_name in window design_info` EVERY TIME THE STARBASE VIEW IS OPENED -- one of only two errors in the 2026-08-07 run that recur during play rather than at load. The block is vanilla's own, copied from interface/starbase_view.gui with vanilla's position and sizing and retabbed to match this file. Anchored on the window's name+position+size together, because the size line alone occurs twice. |
| `sound/ASB_soundeffects.asset` | ASB Ironman | 4.4 wants delay_random_offset and playbackrate_random_offset as a { min max } range; ASB gives a bare 0.0. The same file already writes volume_random_offset = { 0.0 0.15 } correctly, so this is an internal inconsistency rather than a deliberate 3.x form. { 0.0 0.0 } preserves the intended meaning exactly -- no random offset. |
| `sound/advisor_voice_types/STH_advisor_voice_types.txt` | Star Trek: New Horizons | l_vo_rom's weight gates on has_country_flag = romulan_star_empire, which nothing in the build ever sets, so the Romulan advisor voice can never be chosen. Replaced with the species-class check stg_borg_triggers.txt established for the Borg. |

## Renamed files

Vendored files given a different filename by a `renames:` entry in `vendor.yml`. The contents are the source mod's; only the name changed, because within one merged mod the filename is what decides which of two files defining the same key the engine keeps — see `.docs/decisions/27-merge-semantics-per-directory.md`.

*None.*

## Pruned files

Files a source shipped, this build laid down, and the reachability closure then proved nothing in the merged tree names — no sprite, no entity, no `.asset`, no root the engine enters. Removed after the merge by `tools/clutter.py`, re-derived on every `make vendor` rather than listed by hand, and scoped to the tiers where vanilla's own false-positive floor is near zero. `make clutter` reports the same census without removing anything; `clutter_keep:` in `vendor.yml` overrides it per file. See `.docs/decisions/43-clutter-pass.md`.
